title: Prestressed-concrete tendons keep tall capacitor pillars from leaning
idea: Borrowed from prestressed bridges, where tensioned steel keeps concrete in compression: deposit a tensile SiN/TiN liner inside each storage-node cylinder before the mold is removed, so pillars are pre-stressed straight and the multi-level support lattice can be dropped, letting AR reach 100-115 without collapse.
why: Fact 1: leaning and collapse cap capacitor height; dropping 1-2 support-layer litho/etch loops saves capex while raising Cs ~40%.

title: Musician's harmonics: lensless Talbot EUV from a tabletop source
idea: A musician knows a string repeats its pattern at harmonic lengths. Light a periodic array mask with a compact coherent EUV source (laser-driven high harmonics or a compact FEL); the mask self-images at Talbot distances, and achromatic Talbot lithography prints the hole/line lattice at half the mask pitch through a ~100 um gap, with no projection optics.
why: Removes the $100M+ reflective projection optics; tool cost could fall ~10x for periodic layers, opening EUV-class periodic patterning to new suppliers. Risks: source power (throughput) and gap control.

title: Cuttlebone chambers: air-gap tiers on pillars cut coupling and height
idea: Cuttlebone is thin floors separated by gas-filled chambers and tiny pillars; after the tier stack is patterned, dissolve sacrificial carbon or SiGe isolation layers through the slits, leaving air gaps (k=1) held by self-aligned oxide pillars at the bitline holes, then pinch-off seal the slits.
why: Air gaps cut inter-tier coupling ~4x so isolation shrinks from ~30 nm to ~8 nm, about doubling tiers per stack height; with a 50-tier-class process that is ~10x bits/mm2 for one extra wet etch (fact 2).

title: Self-rolling strained films make Swiss-roll capacitors
idea: Inverts 'capacitors are etched into the substrate'. Pattern a strained bilayer (SiNx stressor plus metal/dielectric/metal) at 1 um rules on a sacrificial layer; on release it rolls into a 10-20-turn tube that multiplies plate area per footprint ~20x, then the rolls are anchored and planarized as a capacitor tier.
why: Capacitance from planar 1990s deposition and litho with no high-AR etch (fact 1); rolled-up micro-capacitors exist, per-cell density and contacting are the risk.

title: Strain-driven self-rolling membranes form Swiss-roll capacitors without deep etch
idea: Effect: strain-gradient self-rolling. Put a pre-strained SiNx/TiN/HfO2/TiN stack on a sacrificial Ge strip in each lateral 3D DRAM cell; releasing the strip lets built-in strain roll the stack into a 4-6 turn micro-roll inside the tier cavity, multiplying capacitor area with no vertical etch.
why: Facts 1 and 2: the lateral capacitor blocks 3D DRAM; the rolled shape gives ~5x in-plane area with zero extra litho.

title: Token-sweep restore: inference reads replace refresh, shortening capacitors
idea: TRIZ #25 Self-service: in LLM-inference memory every weight row is activated once per decode step (~10-16 ms) and each activation restores the cell, so the controller disables refresh and guarantees the sweep period; if serving pauses beyond the bound it drops the weights and reloads them from flash, keeping refresh power exactly zero.
why: Zero refresh power and bandwidth (16-33% of idle power, 10-20% of bandwidth today); a guaranteed ~16 ms window vs 64 ms cuts required Cs ~3x, so capacitor AR falls from ~70:1 to ~25:1, deleting support-mesh masks and halving HAR etch time (facts 1, 3, 4).

title: Grown, not implanted: epitaxial n-p-n wafer for vertical cells
idea: Reverse implant-after-pattern into dope-before-pattern: grow the source/channel/drain as an in-situ doped epitaxial stack, etch the pillars with ArF plus SADP, and wrap the wordline gate as a self-aligned spacer, so every critical length is a film thickness.
why: Gives a 4F2 vertical cell without EUV and removes several implant masks; channel length is set within 1 nm by epitaxy, which tightens the leakage tail.

title: F: anhydrous HF vapor dip-out frees capacitor pillars without rinse
idea: Remove the oxide capacitor mold with anhydrous HF plus alcohol vapor at reduced pressure instead of a wet buffered-HF dip, DI rinse and spin-dry; no liquid touches the pillars, so there is no capillary collapse either.
why: Water: the mold dip-out and its rinse go from liters per wafer to ~0 (>10x for the capacitor module); with no stiction, AR can climb past 100:1 for more Cs (fact 1).

title: N: nitrogen-terminated surfaces steer ALD into self-aligned contacts
idea: Expose the wafer to an NH3 plasma chemistry that N-terminates the dielectric but not the Si/metal landing pads, then use precursors that cannot nucleate on N-terminated SiN so liner and contact metal grow only on the pads (area-selective deposition), deleting the contact litho and etch.
why: Fact 4: removes 1-2 mask layers per contact level and their overlay budget; ~3-5% wafer-cost cut and better contact yield at tight pitch.

title: Vertical-channel 6T SRAM built on the 4F² DRAM transistor process
idea: TRIZ #17 Another dimension: reuse the vertical-channel transistor module being developed for 4F2 DRAM, add a complementary p-type pillar, and wire six vertical transistors as a cross-coupled latch in ~24-30F2, skipping the capacitor module entirely.
why: Bistable, so zero refresh; ~5x denser than logic SRAM (~0.004 vs ~0.021 um2/bit) and built in DRAM fabs without the capacitor module (~20-25% fewer steps); ~4x less dense than DRAM, so it targets hot refresh-heavy tiers (facts 3, 4).

title: Dewetted metal nano-islands roughen electrodes into area
idea: Inverts 'the capacitor needs an ordered geometry'. Anneal a 5 nm sacrificial Sn film so it dewets into ~15-25 nm random islands, use them as an RIE mask to texture the poly-Si storage node into nanopillars (the 1990s hemispherical-grain trick taken ~10x further), strip, then coat with dielectric.
why: 5-10x electrode area per footprint from a furnace and an etcher (fact 1), letting thin planar-ish 180 nm-rule caps hold >20 fF.

title: Goto parametrons built in BAW-filter fabs store phase bits
idea: Revive Eiichi Goto's 1954 parametron, which held a bit as the 0 or pi phase of a parametrically pumped resonator, using arrays of ScAlN micro-resonators pumped at 2f by a shared on-chip line; a bit is read by mixing with a reference phase and written by briefly injecting a seed tone. The pump sustains the state, so there is no leaking capacitor and no access-transistor tail.
why: Facts 1 and 3 plus capital: no capacitor etch and no refresh, built in 5-8 mask 150/200 mm BAW-filter fabs that ship billions of parts a year (including U.S. sites). Risks are continuous pump power and ~1 um2 resonators that leave density ~10x below DRAM unless shrunk to NEMS.

title: Airbnb for idle cleanroom tools: memory prototyping by the hour
idea: Borrowed from Airbnb monetizing spare rooms: a 10-person team builds a booking, recipe-transfer and wafer-logistics platform over idle tool hours in U.S. university, national-lab and 200 mm commercial cleanrooms, so memory startups route split lots across ALD at one site, etch at another and test at a third.
why: Capital and time: a new cell concept today needs a ~$50M pilot line; renting tool hours gives 10-50x cheaper, faster learning cycles on U.S. soil.

title: Pay per good bit: vendor-owned DUV litho as a service
idea: Reverse the purchase: the scanner vendor installs and runs DUV tools in the fab and is paid per good die or bit that leaves the litho step, not for the tool.
why: Capital intensity: the fab avoids litho capex and the vendor's incentives match yield; it lowers the entry barrier for no-EUV U.S. fabs.

title: Multi-level DRAM: two bits per capacitor relax lithography
idea: Magnify bits per cell to 2 using four charge levels and a reference-ladder sense amp with refresh-time calibration, buying a node of density without a shrink.
why: Litho-bound scaling: about 2x density at the same F, worth more than a 10-20% node; no new EUV layers.

title: Termite's chemical tunneling: metal-assisted chemical etching of capacitor holes
idea: A biologist watching termites tunnel with saliva sees etching without bombardment. Pattern a Ru or Pt catalyst mesh over a sacrificial silicon mold layer and immerse it in HF/H2O2: the catalyst sinks straight down, digging vertical holes beyond 200:1 at room temperature with no plasma; the catalyst is removed and the holes are lined with electrode/high-k/electrode.
why: Replaces cryogenic/high-AR plasma etchers (~$10-15M each, the slowest step in the flow) with a wet bench, and reaches the AR ~115 needed for >6 fF (fact 1). Risks: catalyst wandering, metal contamination, and stopping exactly on landing pads.

title: Datacenter fleets as ore: reverse-fab reclaim of retired DRAM dies
idea: Scale shift from fab to fleet: DIMMs retired after 4-6 years are laser/chemically decapped, dies are retested and rebinned, then re-assembled onto new substrates or CXL expander cards as capacity-tier memory with stronger ECC.
why: Adds bits with ~zero fab capex; a hyperscaler fleet could recover 30-60% of retired bits at <20% of new-die cost.

title: Eliminate the quartz crucible: electromagnetic cold-crucible silicon crystal growth
idea: Melt silicon in a water-cooled segmented copper crucible where RF induction heats the charge and pushes the melt off the wall (skull melting), so it never touches quartz, and pull 300 mm crystals from it under a magnetic field; oxygen is added only by controlled gas doping.
why: Removes the >80% Spruce Pine high-purity quartz dependence outright and tightens interstitial-oxygen control (fewer slip and precipitate yield losses); cold-crucible casting already exists for solar silicon.

title: Array-only fab: sell bare DRAM arrays to logic foundries
idea: Rearrange the value chain: a U.S. fab makes only array wafers with no periphery, and sells them for bonding to periphery wafers made in an existing logic foundry, like a memory 'fabless in reverse'.
why: Periphery is ~49% of die: the array fab needs about half the masks and none of the logic transistor modules, cutting startup capex ~40% and speeding U.S. entry.

title: Pure-play DRAM foundry with open PDK for fabless designers
idea: Worse: keep the DRAM process locked inside three IDMs. Flip: a DRAM foundry offers an array PDK (cell, capacitor, sense-amp macros) and multi-project wafers, so fabless startups and hyperscalers can tape out custom PIM, wide-I/O or CXL-native DRAM.
why: Capital: spreads utilization over many customers, unlocks designs that do DRAM's job with fewer bits, and opens a U.S. entry path.

title: Fill Optane's empty fab: a toll memory foundry for fabless DRAM
idea: Optane died partly because Intel alone could not fill the Lehi fab, so fixed costs crushed unit cost. Create a memory toll foundry with an open DRAM PDK (cell, sense-amp and redundancy libraries) so AI-chip firms and hyperscalers tape out custom DRAM dies and share one fab's utilization.
why: Capital: >90% utilization across many products instead of one product's swings; amortizes a U.S. fab over many customers; custom dies cut overfetch and periphery waste.

title: Optical-fiber stack-and-draw: sliced silicon-core fiber capacitor plates
idea: Draw a preform of doped-silicon rods in silica (molten-core fiber method), restack and redraw until cores are ~20-30 nm at cell pitch, fuse the bundle into a boule, slice it like an ingot into wafers of vertical Si electrodes in SiO2, recess the silica to expose 1-3 um Si pillars as bottom electrodes, and bond onto the transistor wafer through oversized landing pads that absorb lattice misregistration. Elements: Si, O, B, P.
why: Removes deep etch and EUV for the capacitor layer (facts 1, 4): aspect ratio set by slice thickness, not etch; fiber draw is cheap, continuous and U.S.-strong.

title: Area-selective deposition grows capacitor electrodes up from landing pads
idea: Box: TiN/ZrO2 capacitor charge x standard BCAT x voltage sense amp x 2D x Si x area-selective CVD with inhibitor monolayers. Instead of depositing a 1.5 um mold, etching 70:1 holes and stripping the mold, Ru or TiN pillars grow upward only on the landing pads while the dielectric is inhibitor-passivated, then high-k and top electrode fill around them.
why: Eliminates the highest-AR etch, mold strip and anti-leaning support layers (~8-12 steps and the cryo-etch fleet); claims ~10% wafer cost; risk is selectivity loss over 1 um of growth and lateral mushrooming bridging cells.

title: Page-wide 100,000-nozzle printhead deposits only where needed
idea: Magnify nozzle count to a page-wide MEMS printhead array firing sub-femtoliter drops across the full web, depositing dielectric and electrode only where cells exist instead of blanket coating plus etch.
why: Material and step count: about 95% less material waste, and no litho-etch loop for coarse layers.

title: Eliminate EUV entirely: 4F2 vertical-channel cells at relaxed DUV pitch
idea: Move to a 4F2 vertical-channel-transistor cell but hold F at ~15 nm, which matches the bit area of today's 6F2 at 12 nm and is reachable with immersion DUV plus self-aligned quadruple/octuple patterning. Output is an ordinary DDR5/HBM core die.
why: Fact 4: zero EUV layers at bit-density parity, removing ~$1B+ of scanners per 100k wafers/month and the single-supplier dependency.

title: Thermal-receipt printing: buried metal self-registers the next layer
idea: Like a receipt printer that marks only where heated, flash the wafer with near-IR that buried metal absorbs far more than oxide, so a thermally crosslinking resist hardens only above metal; this registers landing pads to contacts with zero overlay error and no mask, leaving the one allowed new mask for the cut layer.
why: Fact 4: overlay-critical layers without scanner time; overlay error near zero vs the ~2 nm budgets that push layers onto EUV.

title: Vertical printed transistors: channel length set by film thickness
idea: Minify channel length to ~100 nm without fine lithography by building vertical printed transistors in which source and drain are stacked layers and the channel is the coated film thickness.
why: Speed and litho: printed transistors reach switching speeds near what a 10-100 ns DRAM access needs, using only micron-scale patterning.

title: Sideways cell: film thickness, not lithography, sets every dimension
idea: Worse: make every critical dimension depend on optical resolution. Flip: rotate the access transistor 90 degrees so gate length, channel thickness and capacitor dielectric are ALD films grown on the sidewalls of coarse 80 nm DUV trenches. Litho only cuts trenches; Angstrom-precise deposition 'prints' the sub-10 nm features.
why: Litho-bound scaling (fact 4): scaling continues by deposition without EUV, toward ~4F2 at relaxed F.

title: Monk's discipline: three-mask memory tier with spacer-defined vertical TFTs
idea: A monk keeps only what is necessary. Build each tier with three coarse masks: vertical oxide TFTs whose channel length equals a deposited film thickness (~20 nm) on the sidewall of a stepped dielectric, with gate and storage node formed by conformal ALD around the step, so 1 um-class lithography yields 20 nm-class devices at <=350 C.
why: Decouples device size from lithography: ~3 masks per tier vs ~10+, cutting litho cost per tier ~70% and allowing i-line tools. Risks: density limited by contact pitch, sidewall interface leakage.

title: Candle-dipped sidewall channels: ALD thickness sets transistor width
idea: Like dipping candles to build layers on a wick, pattern one mandrel mask, ALD a 3 nm IGZO film on the mandrel sidewalls and etch back so each sidewall becomes a vertical channel whose width is the film thickness; gate dielectric and wordline deposit and recess self-aligned, giving two cells per mandrel.
why: Fact 4: 3 nm device width without EUV; one added mask yields a ~4F2 vertical gain cell above periphery.

title: Open DRAM PDK lets idle U.S. foundries run memory lots
idea: Constraint: no access to incumbent DRAM IP. A public consortium develops and releases a royalty-free 1T1C process kit (recipes, cell, sense amp, redundancy) at a 20-28 nm class on standard logic toolsets, qualified at several U.S. foundries so spare capacity can produce DRAM.
why: U.S. manufacturability and capital: activates depreciated fabs with ~zero new fab capex and breaks the three-company know-how wall.

title: Lithium-niobate acoustic delay block streams KV cache in bulk
idea: Revive the 1950s mercury and quartz acoustic delay lines as a ~1 cm3 block of lithium niobate pulled by Czochralski in air (no argon), with a 2D array of evaporated transducers on one face launching 2-5 GHz bulk waves that reflect and recirculate; each transducer channel holds ~1-2 kbit per transit. LLM decoding reads the KV cache in fixed order every token, matching a delay line's access pattern.
why: Capital and the constraint: ~2 masks for transducers and no rare gas anywhere; 1e5-1e6 channels per block could hold ~1 Gb at >10 TB/s sequential bandwidth. Risks are GHz acoustic attenuation, transducer crosstalk and ~1-2 us worst-case latency.

title: Eliminate the capacitor-hole mask: block-copolymer self-assembly guided by landing pads
idea: Coat a cylinder-forming block copolymer over the landing-pad topography so it self-assembles into a hexagonal hole array registered to the pads, and use it directly as the hard-mask template for capacitor holes. The die and its DDR5/HBM interface are unchanged.
why: Replaces one EUV or 2-3 DUV multipatterning exposures with a spin and bake, and tightens hole-CD uniformity, narrowing Cs variation.

title: LTPS excimer-laser crystallization builds polysilicon tiers at low temperature
idea: Borrowed from AMOLED backplanes, which turn amorphous Si into polysilicon with line-beam excimer lasers without heating the glass: deposit a-Si for each 3D DRAM tier and laser-crystallize it in nanoseconds, so tiers stack on finished CMOS and earlier tiers within BEOL thermal budgets.
why: Fact 2: the lateral transistor blocks 3D DRAM; display ELA tools already process 3 m2 glass, give ~100 cm2/Vs mobility and skip the costly Si/SiGe epitaxial superlattice.

title: Electric-eel electrocyte stacks: shallow nanolaminate capacitors replace tall pillars
idea: Electric eels reach high output by stacking thousands of thin electrocytes; ALD-stack 8-12 alternating Ru/ZrO2 layers in a shallow ~150 nm recess and tie odd and even electrodes to node and plate through two self-aligned sidewall spacers, like a miniature multilayer ceramic capacitor.
why: Capacitor area multiplies by layer count without high-AR etching (fact 1); removes the 60:1 etch and support layers, est. 8-10% lower wafer cost and lower etch capex.

title: MicroLED mass transfer: printing known-good DRAM array tiles
idea: Borrow microLED micro-transfer printing: build ~200 um DRAM array tiles on a donor wafer, test them, then elastomer-stamp only known-good tiles onto periphery wafers at the sense-amp interface; failed sites are re-printed as microLED repair does.
why: Yield and capital: die yield becomes tile yield (~99%+), letting new fabs run aggressive cells profitably at low yield, shrinking redundancy and fuse area, and letting several small fabs feed one assembler.

title: Aircraft-leasing model for scanners and etchers
idea: Copy AerCap/GECAS: a lessor buys scanners, etchers and deposition tools in bulk, leases them to fabs on 5-8 year operating leases with standard return conditions and maintenance reserves, and re-markets returned tools to the next fab, including startups and mini-fabs.
why: Capital intensity (depreciation ~55% of wafer cost): turns capex into opex, lowers the entry barrier for new U.S. entrants, and bulk purchasing plus secondary-market liquidity lowers lease rates.

title: Revive the 1990s BST bet: planar k~250 capacitors
idea: Inverts 'more charge needs taller capacitors'. Deposit (Ba,Sr)TiO3 by MOCVD or sol-gel on Pt/Ru electrodes, the material of the 1990s Gbit-DRAM programs, with compositional grading to cut leakage; at k ~250 a 44 nm planar film stores 5 fF in 0.1 um2.
why: Takes fact 1's k~70 escape route with ~3x margin and no high-AR etch, using only 1990s deposition tools.

title: Dielectrophoresis drops pre-made capacitor rods into transistor-wafer sockets
idea: Effect: dielectrophoresis. Coaxial TiN/ZrO2/TiN capacitor nanorods are batch-made off-wafer by template electroplating and ALD, released into a fluid, and trapped one per socket by an AC field between bitline-contact electrodes, then anneal-bonded in place.
why: Separates the most capital-heavy module (the HAR capacitor) from the FEOL fab, and batch rods cost cents per wafer-equivalent. Placement yield must exceed 99.9999%.

title: Strain-driven rolled-up nanomembrane capacitors on glass
idea: Worse: build capacitors as ever-taller, fragile pillars. Flip: deposit a pre-strained bilayer carrying an electrode/high-k/electrode stack on a sacrificial layer over glass, then release it so it self-rolls into a Swiss-roll capacitor about 10 windings deep. This multiplies plate area per footprint without deep etching.
why: Capacitor charge wall: effective AR above 100 by rolling, with no high-AR etch and no pattern collapse.

title: Micro-transfer printing 100 um DRAM chiplets onto panels
idea: Minify the die to 100 um chiplets made at a mature node, then magnify deployment by elastomer-stamp transfer printing 100,000 chiplets per stroke onto large panels with printed interconnect.
why: Yield and capital: tiny dies yield near 100%, mature nodes avoid EUV, and panel-scale assembly replaces per-die packaging.

title: Optical-fiber preform drawing: coaxial capacitors drawn, bundled, sliced
idea: Borrowed from telecom fiber drawing and multimaterial fibers, which shrink a 10 cm preform 10,000x: draw a preform of packed coaxial metal/glass-dielectric/metal rods to ~50 nm cores, bundle and redraw, then slice the bundle into 1-5 um discs; each disc is a ready-made capacitor array, with aspect ratio set by slice thickness, bonded onto a transistor wafer.
why: Facts 1/4: zero lithography and zero high-AR etch for the capacitor, AR 100+ for free; core uniformity and registration to transistors are speculative.

title: Fluorine-free molybdenum wordlines grown barrier-less from chloride precursors
idea: Under 125 C for 10 years: deposit Mo from MoO2Cl2 directly on the wordline gate oxide with no TiN barrier and no fluorine, so there is no fluorine to attack the oxide, and the freed barrier volume goes to a thicker, longer-lived gate dielectric.
why: Tungsten chokepoint removed; better time-dependent breakdown at 125 C; resistance ~-30% at buried-wordline dimensions.

title: Full-wafer single-shot nanoimprint of each array layer
idea: Magnify the imprint field from one 26x33 mm die to the whole 300 mm wafer: a flexible quartz-on-glass master imprints every array layer in a single press using thermal-expansion-matched chucks and in-situ moire alignment.
why: Lithography throughput and tool cost: one press per wafer replaces ~100 scanner shots; tool cost ~$15-30M versus ~$200M EUV, targeting >5x lower litho cost per wafer layer.

title: Run vertical gain-cell DRAM through idle 3D NAND fab lines
idea: First principle: most of the capital in a 3D NAND fab is alternating-stack deposition, high-AR channel-hole etch and staircase formation, which is exactly the tool set needed for a vertical-channel 2T0C gain cell: a stack of horizontal wordline layers pierced by oxide-semiconductor channels. Port the NAND flow (ONON stack, channel hole, replacement gate) to a gain-cell DRAM so NAND overcapacity in down-cycles produces DRAM with no new tools.
why: Capital intensity and time (facts 2, 4): reuses tens of $B of installed NAND capacity with no EUV; capacity in ~12 months instead of 3-5 years.

title: N: cryogenic nitrogen aerosol lifts particles with zero liquid
idea: Sweep an expanding jet of N2/Ar cryogenic aerosol (frozen micro-particles) across the wafer so momentum transfer lifts nanoparticles, after which the aerosol sublimes with no residue; use it wherever megasonic DI scrubs are used today.
why: Water: particle-removal scrubs drop to zero water, and the gentle dry action avoids toppling fragile capacitor pillars.

title: Wireless charging coils: TSV-free inductively stacked HBM
idea: Borrow Qi chargers and RFID near-field links: stack thinned DRAM dies without TSVs, pass data through on-chip aluminum spiral coils across ~10 um adhesive layers at Gb/s per coil, and bring power through a few wide edge or through-mold vias.
why: HBM TSV tax (fact 6: ~3x area per bit, -20-30% yield): removes TSV etch, Cu fill with Ta barriers and keep-out zones, moving stacked memory back toward DDR5 area efficiency.

title: Spot-color fifth plate: one-mask IGZO gain cell in logic BEOL
idea: Treat a logic flow as a four-color press and add exactly one spot-color plate: one mask patterns an ALD IGZO island between Mn and Mn+1, the existing Mn line serves as bottom gate, and redrawn (not added) via masks form source/drain and read contacts, making a 2T0C gain cell any logic foundry can offer.
why: U.S. manufacturability/capital: DRAM-class embedded memory on existing logic capacity for +1 mask (~3% wafer cost), with no capacitor module and no EUV.

title: Stress-limited oxidation self-equalizes pillar diameters from sloppy cheap litho
idea: Effect: stress-retarded oxidation at high curvature. Pattern Si pillars with relaxed, high-LWR ArF or imprint litho, then wet-oxidize at ~850 C: compressive stress at small radii slows oxidation, so all pillars converge to a uniform 8-10 nm core whatever their starting diameter. Strip the oxide to get uniform vertical channels.
why: Facts 3 and 4: channel-diameter spread feeds the leakage tail; a physics-based CD equalizer lets patterning with 3x worse CD control still reach tight Vt distributions.

title: Nanosecond protonic gain cell stores bits as ions, BEOL-only
idea: Ideal: memory where nothing leaks because the state is atoms, not electrons. Closest: a BEOL transistor whose MoO3 or TiO2 channel conductance is set by nanosecond proton insertion from a thin solid electrolyte (PSG) gate, giving a volatile-to-hours state with non-destructive read; three DUV masks at <400 C, no capacitor.
why: Facts 1, 3, 4: no capacitor and slow refresh, stackable in BEOL tiers on any logic wafer; tungsten-free channel avoids the W chokepoint.

title: Charge-coupled shift-register memory revived with spacer-patterned gates
idea: Ideal: a memory with no per-cell transistor and no capacitor. Closest: rebuild 1970s CCD memory as many short (32-64-bit) recirculating loops of overlapping gate electrodes formed by self-aligned double patterning on DUV; charge packets in surface potential wells are clocked past one shared sense/restore amplifier per loop.
why: Facts 1, 3, 4, 7: removes access transistors and capacitors, makes refresh part of recirculation, ~2-3F2 per bit at DUV pitch; ~20-30 ns average latency at GHz clocking, with clocking energy as the main risk.

title: Biologist's self-ordering pores: anodic alumina as capacitor molds
idea: Diatoms grow perfect hexagonal pores with no blueprint. Deposit thick aluminum over the array, pre-dimple it with a coarse imprint, and anodize: pores self-order into a hexagonal lattice at ~30-60 nm pitch with aspect ratios beyond 200:1, which become the mold for cylinder capacitors (ALD electrode/high-k/electrode inside), with the alumina stripped or kept as a mechanical support.
why: Replaces the capacitor-hole litho layer and the $10M+ high-AR plasma etch with a wet bath; AR >115 attacks the charge wall (fact 1) and capex at once. Risks: registering pores to landing pads, and opening the barrier at the pore bottom.

title: Spider-spinneret thermal drawing shrinks a macro preform into nanocell arrays
idea: Spiders draw nanoscale fibers from a gland; assemble a centimetre-scale preform of chalcogenide-glass channel, low-melting metal electrodes and polymer dielectric in the exact cell pattern, thermally draw it ~10^4x like optical fiber to ~20 nm features, then bundle, fuse and slice the fibers crosswise into thin 'memory wafers' that are hybrid-bonded onto CMOS.
why: Feature size comes from draw ratio, not lithography; one cheap preform yields kilometres of fiber, so slices can reach ~10x bits/mm2 at bulk-material cost with zero masks (fact 4).

title: CFET-stacked two-transistor gain cell from an unmodified logic flow
idea: Ideal: memory that costs zero extra masks in a logic fab. Closest: in a CFET (n-over-p stacked nanosheet) process, the top sheet is a high-Vt write transistor and the bottom sheet a read transistor whose gate is the storage node, giving a capacitorless 2T gain cell in one transistor footprint using only a layout change.
why: Facts 1 and 4, U.S. manufacturability: zero added steps and no capacitor module; any CFET logic fab, including U.S. ones, becomes a DRAM-class source; ~2x denser than planar 2T eDRAM.

title: Dolan-bridge angled evaporation forms self-aligned sub-litho features
idea: Revive Dolan's 1977 suspended-resist-bridge shadow evaporation, used to make Josephson junctions: one coarse imprint forms a resist bridge, and two evaporations at opposite angles in high vacuum (oxidation in O2, no argon milling) deposit overlapping strips whose overlap width is set by angle and bridge height rather than litho. Use it for ~10 nm gate-to-contact overlaps and narrow metal strips.
why: Fact 4: turns a high-resolution litho layer into a coarse layer plus geometry, removing EUV or immersion passes on self-aligned structures; e-beam evaporators cost ~$1-2M and need no rare gas. Risks are throughput and step coverage.

title: DNA-brick 3D crystals cast an entire multi-tier cell array
idea: Grow micron-thick 3D DNA-brick crystals (programmed voxel lattices at ~2.5 nm resolution) on the CMOS wafer from anchor pads, with designed voids forming the channel, wordline and bitline network of a 6-tier gain-cell array; infiltrate by sequential ALD (In2O3, HfO2, TiN/Ru) and burn out the DNA to leave a ceramic-metal cast.
why: All tiers are patterned at ~8 nm pitch by one self-assembly step and no masks; 6 tiers x ~2x lateral shrink is ~10x+ bits/mm2, at flat cost if enzymatic DNA synthesis reaches <$50 per wafer (fact 4).

title: Thermally decomposable polynorbornene air-gap bitlines boost sensing margin
idea: Extreme user: 0.5 V energy-harvesting IoT that needs a large sense signal. Fill between bitlines with a sacrificial polynorbornene that decomposes cleanly at ~425C through a porous cap, leaving air gaps with no fluorinated low-k or HF release.
why: Capacitor wall: bitline capacitance falls ~30-40%, so the same signal needs ~30% less Cs, allowing shorter pillars and an easier capacitor etch.

title: Josephson-era missing memory: 77 K thin-oxide 3D NAND as DRAM
idea: IBM's Josephson program (cancelled 1983) and later cryogenic computing stalled for lack of dense, cheap cold memory. At 77 K leakage collapses, so a 3D NAND-style vertical string with a 1.5-2 nm direct-tunneling oxide instead of ~7 nm Fowler-Nordheim oxide programs at ~3-5 V in tens of ns, suffers little hot-carrier wear and holds charge for hours.
why: Meets 100x: NAND cost structure (~$0.03-0.08/GB) with near-DRAM write speed, refresh-free hours retention and ~1e12-class endurance. Trade: liquid-nitrogen cooling (~10-15% facility overhead).

title: IBM racetrack grown in anodized-alumina pores with zero bit-scale lithography
idea: IBM's racetrack memory died because nobody could fabricate its vertical 3D magnetic nanowires. Anodize aluminium into self-ordered 30-60 nm pores tens of um deep, pulse-electroplate Co/Ni-Cu modulated nanowires whose composition steps act as domain-wall pinning notches (~100 bits per wire), and read pore clusters holding majority-voted copies through a coarse MTJ crossbar underneath.
why: Meets 100x: no lithography at bit scale, only anodizing and plating baths, ~100 bits stacked per pore; est. <$0.05/GB vs ~$5-10/GB DRAM. Trades: 50-500 ns shift latency and sequential bias (good for streaming AI weights), redundancy overhead.

title: Self-ordering anodized-alumina pores as litho-free capacitor molds
idea: Ideal: capacitor holes that pattern themselves. Closest: anodize a thick Al film over the cell array, seeded by shallow DUV-imprinted dimples on the storage-contact grid, so it self-orders into the same honeycomb lattice DRAM already uses (25-35 nm pitch, >100:1 pores); ALD TiN/ZrO2/TiN lines the pores, replacing the capacitor-mold lithography and high-aspect-ratio dry etch.
why: Facts 1 and 4: removes one critical litho layer and the most expensive HAR plasma etch; AR ~115 becomes cheap, so Cs +40-50%; est. 5-8% wafer-cost cut in the capacitor module.

title: Photopatternable hafnium-oxo resist that becomes the functional film
idea: TRIZ #32 Color changes (change a substance's properties): use a Hf/Zr oxo-cluster resist that, after exposure and development, is annealed straight into dense HfO2/ZrO2 that stays as a hardmask, spacer or isolation layer, so the patterned film is never etched.
why: Collapses deposit-coat-expose-etch-strip into coat-expose-develop-anneal, saving ~3-4 steps per use and some etch chambers (process steps, tool cost).

title: Crystal planes, not lithography, define atomically flat vertical channels
idea: Constraint: nothing finer than 80 nm may be printed for the active area. On (110) wafers, anisotropic TMAH etching exposes vertical {111} walls, so coarse 80 nm lines are wet-thinned to 8-10 nm fins whose sidewalls are crystal planes, then cut into pillars for vertical-channel access transistors.
why: Facts 3 and 4: removes EUV/SAQP from active definition; near-zero line-edge roughness tightens the leakage tail ~2x; the wet etch costs a few dollars per wafer.

title: Compact-synchrotron X-ray proximity lithography for DRAM array layers
idea: Revive the 1990s IBM/NTT X-ray proximity lithography programme, dropped in favour of optics, with compact storage-ring sources (~1 nm wavelength) and 1:1 membrane masks at a few um gap, combined with spacer pitch division to print DRAM's periodic arrays. One ring can feed 10-20 exposure ports.
why: EUV single-supplier risk and capital (Fact 4): a ring plus several X-ray steppers built from U.S. accelerator know-how could print the 5-7 critical layers for less than the ~$200M+ per EUV scanner; risks are 1:1 mask making and overlay.

title: DRAM bit futures exchange to end memory-cycle bankruptcies
idea: Qimonda (2009) and Elpida (2012) were killed by price troughs, not technology. Create exchange-cleared monthly futures per Gb of DDR5-equivalent bits so fabs hedge 2-3 years of output and banks lend against hedged revenue as with oil producers, while buyers hedge shortages.
why: Capital: removes the boom-bust risk premium that inflates financing and causes over/under-build; a few points lower cost of capital and steadier utilization worth ~10-15% of wafer cost.

title: Three-mask crosspoint capacitor arrays stacked in 28 nm BEOL
idea: Po: memory with only three masks. Build stacked tiers of 1-selector-1-capacitor crosspoint cells (threshold-switch selector plus thin-film capacitor at each line crossing) in a mature foundry's BEOL with two line masks and one via mask per tier.
why: Mask count and density in trailing fabs: 4F2 per tier at F=40 nm, ~8 tiers to approach leading-node density; risk is selector off-leakage forcing ms-scale refresh.

title: Cold-crucible Czochralski: silicon contains itself, no quartz consumed
idea: First principle: the quartz crucible is consumed only because it touches molten Si at 1414 C, but molten Si can sit in a thin frozen skin of its own Si inside a segmented, water-cooled copper crucible heated by induction. Grow DRAM-grade crystals by skull-melting CZ; the copper crucible is repaired and reused indefinitely, and the skull is remelted into the next charge.
why: Spruce Pine (>80%) quartz-crucible chokepoint: removes the consumable, and less oxygen dissolves into the crystal.

title: One-hole cell: capacitor and vertical oxide transistor share one hole
idea: Box: MIM charge at hole bottom x vertical IGZO channel lining the hole top x voltage sense amp x BEOL over periphery x Si x single etched hole with sequential ALD fill and recess. One hole receives bottom electrode and high-k, is recessed, then gets a lined IGZO channel and gate-all-around wordline fill, so storage-node contacts, landing pads and their overlay steps disappear.
why: Mask count and overlay (fact 4): removes 3-4 masks including EUV contacts, natively 4F2, and sits over periphery (fact 7); risk is IGZO quality on the hole sidewall and series resistance.

title: Inverted fin capacitor: storage discs between continuous plate sheets
idea: Under 125 C for 10 years: deposit a ~20-layer stack of continuous plate metal sheets alternating with sacrificial layers, etch one hole per cell, laterally recess the sacrificial layers into rings and fill dielectric plus storage metal, giving a stack of storage discs interleaved with the plates.
why: Facts 1 and 4: ~3-6 fF at AR ~15 instead of 70, so the extra charge for 125 C retention comes from deposition, not from the hardest etch.

title: Used Blu-ray mastering lasers write 40 nm imprint masters by heat-mode
idea: Effect: thermal-threshold nonlinearity. Buy two retired 405 nm Blu-ray mastering rigs (~$150k each), swap the spindle for a used XY air-bearing stage, and coat masters with a phase-change resist (AgInSbTe or Ge-Sb-Te): only the center of the Gaussian spot passes the crystallization threshold, so ~40 nm marks are written and then wet-etched selectively. The rest of the $1M funds 24 months of DRAM-array NIL master demos.
why: Masks and capital: e-beam-written NIL masters cost $0.5-1M+ each; a ~$400k heat-mode writer cuts master cost >10x and gives the U.S. its own master supply.

title: Shape-memory NiTi microsprings close warped HBM gaps on heating
idea: Effect: martensitic shape-memory recovery with thermal hysteresis. Sputter NiTi micro-bumps trained as compressed springs; heating above the austenite finish temperature makes each bump extend 1-3 um to meet its pad and absorb die warpage, and the hysteresis keeps them extended at operating temperature. $1M covers the target, university MEMS line time and a 24-month reliability demo.
why: Fact 6: warpage forces costly TCB and CMP-flat hybrid bonding with 20-30% yield loss; compliant self-actuating bumps raise stack yield on cheaper bonders.

title: Plasmonic contact printing with UV LEDs and disposable masks
idea: Revive 1970s contact printing, abandoned because masks wore out, with two 2026 fixes: each wafer gets a disposable conformal mask nanoimprinted from a master, and a 365 nm UV-LED source excites surface plasmons in the mask's silver layer so near-field exposure resolves ~22 nm half-pitch. No laser gas and no mercury-lamp argon or xenon fill is involved.
why: Fact 4 under the constraint: ~$2-5M tools versus ~$60M immersion or $200M+ EUV for DRAM's periodic layers. Risks are contact defects, overlay and the ~20 nm plasmonic depth of field.

title: Backside-power flow repurposed to build capacitors behind the transistors
idea: Combine backside-power-delivery/BSI wafer thinning with the 1T1C cell: access transistors and bitlines are built on the front, the wafer is bonded to a carrier and thinned to the channel bottoms, and the storage capacitors are formed on the exposed backside drains, so bitline and capacitor no longer compete for one plane.
why: Decouples capacitor thermal budget and geometry from bitline routing, enabling a 4F2 cell at relaxed F (~15 nm rather than 12 nm) and removing ~2 EUV-critical self-aligned contact steps; ~30% density at the same litho (facts 1, 4).

title: Ballroom-free fab: ISO-1 microenvironments inside an ISO-7 shell
idea: TRIZ #35 Parameter changes moves cleanliness from the building to the wafer: sealed FOUPs, nitrogen-purged EFEMs and tool-integrated ISO-1 microenvironments carry all contamination control, while the building is a cheap ISO-7 warehouse with ordinary HVAC.
why: Cleanroom shell and HVAC are ~20-30% of fab construction cost and set much of the 3-5 year build; could cut shell capex ~50% and time-to-first-wafer by ~1 year (capital).

title: Gen-8.5 LCD lines plus panel nanoimprint for oxide gain-cell tiles
idea: Combine written-off display-TFT fabs (oxide sputter and 2.2x2.5 m glass handling) with panel-scale nanoimprint at ~200 nm rules, and build 2T0C oxide gain-cell tiles on glass. The tiles are diced and bonded as a slow capacity tier (~50-100 ns) for cold KV-cache and embeddings.
why: Panel area costs 50-100x less per cm2 than 300 mm wafer area and needs no new capex, no EUV and no HPQ crucibles. Even at ~1 um2 cells, it adds bit supply outside the wafer-fab bottleneck (capital intensity, scarce resources).

title: Substitute water rinse-dry with supercritical CO2 for high-AR capacitor arrays
idea: Replace DI-water rinse and dry after capacitor mold strip with supercritical CO2 plus co-solvents, which has zero surface tension, so ultra-high-AR electrode cylinders cannot lean or stick together. This deletes the mid- and top-level nitride support meshes (two patterning steps) and allows AR >100.
why: Fact 1: pattern collapse limits capacitor AR; also cuts ultrapure-water use for these steps by a large fraction.

title: Grow capacitor electrodes upward by selective-area growth
idea: First principle: selective deposition happens only where surface chemistry allows, and unlike etch its rate does not depend on aspect ratio. Build the storage node bottom-up: selective-area MOCVD of conductive RuO2 or TiN nanopillars only on exposed storage-node contacts through a thin 100 nm template, braced by a lattice of nitride support rings, then wrap with high-k and a top plate.
why: Capacitor wall (fact 1) and etch capex: removes the 1.5 um mold deposition, high-AR mold etch and mold strip; pillar height is limited by bracing, not by etch physics.

title: Ashable carbon capacitor mold removed dry, ending pillar collapse
idea: Ideal: the capacitor mold vanishes without touching the pillars. Closest: build the pillar mold from amorphous carbon instead of oxide, so after electrode ALD it is removed by an O2/N2 plasma ash rather than an HF dip-out, eliminating capillary pillar collapse, supercritical-CO2 drying and the nitride support-mesh lithography.
why: Facts 1 and 4: AR can rise from ~70 toward ~100 without collapse (Cs +30-40%), deletes one mask (support mesh) plus wet/dry steps, and removes a top yield-excursion source.

title: Butterfly-scale gyroid electrodes grown inside lipid cubic-phase templates
idea: Butterfly scales grow gyroid networks from folded cell membranes; fill a shallow ~300 nm capacitor well with a monoolein lipid cubic phase (a self-forming gyroid with 5-10 nm water channels), electrodeposit Ru through the channels, wash out the lipid and ALD-coat the bicontinuous electrode with high-k and plate. Surface area per volume rises ~15-20x.
why: Reaches ~5 fF in a 4-5:1 well instead of a 60-75:1 pillar (fact 1), deleting the costliest high-AR etch and support layers; est. ~10% lower wafer cost and less etch-tool capex.

title: Flip the wafer: build capacitors on the backside
idea: Inverts 'capacitors sit above bitlines on the front'. After front-side transistors and bitlines, bond to a carrier, thin to ~0.5 um and open storage-node contacts from the back directly onto source/drain, building capacitors over the full cell footprint with no bitlines in the way.
why: Removes the buried-contact and landing-pad layers that snake past bitlines (1-2 EUV layers) and gives ~1.5x capacitor footprint, so AR can drop ~30% (facts 1, 4).

title: Tie-dye wicking: slit-fed lateral diffusion dopes every tier at once
idea: Like dye wicking into folded cloth, use the single added slit mask to cut through the 3D DRAM tier stack, fill slits with doped glass or vapor dopant, and drive a timed lateral diffusion that forms source/drain junctions in all tiers simultaneously, setting channel length by diffusion distance.
why: Fact 2: lateral-transistor junctions for 50+ tiers in one step, where per-tier implants are impossible; no per-tier masks.

title: Colloidal nanosphere lattice patterns transistors and capacitors in register
idea: Combine nanosphere lithography with a vertical-channel 4F2 cell. A monolayer of ~25 nm beads, guided by coarse immersion-printed trenches so rows stay straight, defines the pillar transistors, and the same lattice, shrunk by etch, defines the capacitors above. The ~1% bead vacancies and dislocations are simply bad cells.
why: Removes 3-5 critical array masks and all array overlay steps, so array patterning capex collapses to coaters plus one coarse layer (fact 4).

title: Test storage nodes mid-flow through a sacrificial wiring layer
idea: Inverts 'electrical test happens at the end'. Right after capacitor formation, deposit a temporary metal grid that ties storage nodes into addressable test groups, map shorts and leakers with a probe card in minutes, strip it, and feed the map to redundancy planning and scrap/rework before the costly BEOL.
why: Stops spending ~40% of remaining process cost on doomed wafers and cuts yield-learning loops from ~3 months to ~1 (fact 4 capital efficiency).

title: Zero-extra-mask eDRAM from stacked metal-finger capacitors in logic BEOL
idea: Extreme user: $1 MCUs that need 1-32 MB on-die. Store charge in interdigitated metal-oxide-metal fringe capacitors stacked through 6-8 standard logic metal layers, read by a 2T gain cell, so any logic flow gets DRAM without a single added mask or tool.
why: Capital: offloads small-memory demand to every logic fab at zero added masks; no EUV and no capacitor module.

title: Magnetostrictive actuators correct nanoimprint template distortion in situ
idea: Effect: magnetostriction. Galfenol or Terfenol-D thin-film actuators along the imprint template frame are driven by a coil array under the chuck, deforming the template by nanometers without contact to correct magnification and trapezoid errors field by field, with hysteresis compensation in the controller.
why: Fact 4: overlay is what keeps NIL from replacing EUV on DRAM layers; sub-2 nm overlay would move 2-3 layers to NIL at ~1/3 the EUV cost of ownership.

title: Bloch-line memory: bits smaller than the lithography defining them
idea: Revive NEC and JPL's 1980s Bloch-line memory, where bits are pairs of vertical Bloch lines inside the walls of litho-defined stripe domains, using modern ferrimagnetic garnet or PMA multilayer films and spin-orbit-torque pulses to shift the lines along the walls. Lithography only draws stripes at ~100 nm; the film's exchange length (~10 nm) sets bit pitch along each wall.
why: Litho-bound scaling (Fact 4): a ~10x density multiplier over drawn pitch, so arrays could be patterned with i-line/KrF on 200 mm tools instead of EUV. Risks are speed (historically microseconds) and Bloch-line stability at 10 nm.

title: Ten-million-beam maskless e-beam wafer writer
idea: Magnify the beam count of multibeam mask writers by 100x to 10 million individually blanked beams on a MEMS aperture plate, with array rasters stored as one repeated tile, so DRAM layers are written maskless at ~50 wafers/hour.
why: EUV single-supplier risk and mask cost: removes EUV and multi-million-dollar mask sets; a US-buildable electron-optics tool chain.

title: Pressure-cooker deuterium anneal to upgrade leaky DRAM wafers
idea: Borrowed from pressure cookers, which speed cooking with pressure: a small team runs a 20 atm deuterium furnace at ~400 C on retention-fallout DRAM wafers, driving D into the Si/SiO2 interface traps behind the leakage tail (Si-D bonds resist breaking far better than Si-H), then re-tests and re-bins them.
why: Fact 3: shrinking the leakage tail can stretch refresh 2-4x and rescue otherwise scrapped die; a high-pressure anneal vessel is a modest, small-team-buildable tool.

title: Nacre-style perovskite nanosheet tiling gives room-temperature k~200 dielectrics
idea: Nacre is brick-and-mortar layering; tile exfoliated Ca2Nb3O10 or Sr-niobate nanosheets (k 200+ at ~2 nm) by Langmuir-Blodgett or electrophoretic layer-by-layer deposition, with a one-molecule polycation 'mortar' between bricks, from water dispersions below 100 C in a dip tool.
why: k~200 vs ~40 for ZrO2 stacks roughly quadruples charge per area (fact 1, target k~70), cutting capacitor height ~3-4x; dip tools cost <1/10 of ALD clusters.

title: Lego-key bonding: etched studs self-align dies without precision bonders
idea: Use the single added mask to etch tapered studs on the DRAM die and matching sockets on the base wafer; a cheap micron-accurate placer drops dies and gentle vibration seats them so the mechanical keys pull overlay below 100 nm before hybrid bonding.
why: Capital/Fact 6: replaces ~$5M sub-200 nm hybrid bonders with pick-and-place at ~1/5 the cost and several times the throughput.

title: Open repair-port mandate lets anyone rebin and repair DRAM
idea: First principle: every DRAM already holds spare rows and post-package-repair fuses; only the access is closed. Create a JEDEC standard and a procurement rule requiring a documented, authenticated repair interface (PPR, fuse map, test modes) on all DRAM, so third parties can repair and rebin used and marginal parts.
why: Usable supply: part of discarded and marginal DRAM becomes usable stock; enables reverse-fab businesses.

title: Printing-press nanoimprint drum for continuous wafer streams
idea: Magnify lithography throughput 20x by passing wafers on a conveyor under a rotating nanoimprint drum carrying the array pattern, printing one layer per second like a newspaper press.
why: Litho tool cost and throughput: ~3600 wafer-layers per hour versus ~150 for EUV, from a drum tool costing a fraction of a scanner.

title: Metal-assisted chemical etching carves 100:1 capacitor trenches without plasma
idea: Box: Si trench charge x planar Si MOSFET access x standard sensing x 2D x Si x MacEtch with an EBL-patterned noble-metal mesh in HF/H2O2. The catalytic film sinks vertically into Si at room temperature, carving smooth high-AR holes in a wet bench; the catalyst is stripped and holes are lined by ALD.
why: Highest-AR etch with no plasma tool or helium-cooled chuck (AR >100 shown in research); capex <$10k; risk is catalyst contamination in a DRAM-grade flow and verticality below 50 nm.

title: Node-freeze fab with 15-year depreciation
idea: Reverse the roadmap: freeze one mature node and run it 15+ years, drawing cost-down from yield, cycle time and tool reuse instead of shrinks; tools are depreciated straight-line over 15 years, not 5.
why: Depreciation share of wafer cost falls from ~55% to ~20-25%, giving 30-40% cost-per-wafer cut, larger than a node shrink's 10-20% per-bit gain.

title: Temporary-bond tester wafer probes every die in one touch
idea: Combine temporary direct bonding with wafer probing: a reusable tester wafer carrying BIST controllers and power delivery is bonded face-to-face to the DRAM wafer through the fine-pitch pads later used for stacking. It runs all die tests in parallel and then debonds.
why: Probe cards and ATE are ~10% of DRAM capex. Whole-wafer parallel test cuts tester count and test time ~10x and makes known-good die for HBM cheaper (fact 6).

title: Surface chemistry inherits one mask through four self-aligned layers
idea: Shift patterning from the reticle to the monolayer: after a single bitline exposure, small-molecule inhibitors (aminosilanes on oxide, thiols on metal) bind to only one surface type, so area-selective ALD grows plugs, landing pads and caps exactly on prior features with no new masks.
why: Removes 3-4 masks and their overlay budget per array (~10% fewer litho passes) and cuts edge-placement failures (Fact 4).

title: Hard-drive flying heads become plasmonic lithography writers
idea: Borrow from storage at rack scale: a Minnesota-made HDD slider carrying a plasmonic ridge aperture flies ~10 nm above a spinning resist-coated wafer at ~10 m/s and writes ~20 nm features with near-field light; 100+ heads write the periodic array as concentric tracks.
why: Maskless sub-20 nm patterning from an all-domestic HDD supply chain at ~1% of EUV tool cost (Fact 4).

title: Bit-forward securities pre-sell future DRAM to finance fabs
idea: Po: the fab is paid for with memory not yet made. Issue tradable forward contracts on standardized gigabit deliveries 3-5 years out, bought by hyperscalers, OEMs and funds, financing ~50% of capex before groundbreaking and settling physically or against a price index.
why: Capital intensity and cyclicality: moves capex risk to buyers who need supply, lowers cost of capital ~3-5 points and breaks boom-bust underinvestment.

title: Half-height capacitors: 2.5 fF cells sensed with code-assisted margin
idea: Combine a 30:1 capacitor mold, half today's height, with an offset-cancelling sense amp and the 1% error budget. Cs halves to ~2.5 fF, and the weakest ~1% of cells that mis-sense are left to the code.
why: Halves HAR etch time on the costliest tool fleet, removes one or two support lattices and reduces mold collapse; ~8-10% wafer cost and ~2x etch throughput (facts 1, 4).

title: Square panels for HBM stacking and bonding
idea: Rearrange the substrate shape: after front-end, re-tile known-good DRAM dies onto 510x515 mm rectangular panels for hybrid bonding, thinning, TSV reveal and molding instead of round 300 mm reconstituted wafers.
why: HBM TSV tax: ~3-4x more dies per back-end pass, panel tool cost per unit area ~50% lower, raises stacking throughput.

title: Glancing-angle-deposited nanohelix electrodes multiply capacitor area, maskless
idea: Box: MIM charge on a 3D nanocolumn electrode x standard access x standard sensing x 2D x Si x glancing-angle e-beam evaporation at ~85 degrees with substrate rotation. Self-shadowing grows isolated TiN or Ru columns or helices of set height on EBL-seeded storage pads, then ALD dielectric and top electrode coat them for 5-20x area with no high-AR etch.
why: Capacitor wall (fact 1) by additive self-shadowing instead of etching; needs only an evaporator with a motorized stage; risk is column porosity raising leakage and fill conformality.

title: Floating nanosphere monolayers mask capacitor holes without scanners
idea: Scale shift to colloids: U.S.-synthesized 25-30 nm silica nanospheres self-pack as a hexagonal monolayer on a Langmuir trough, transfer onto the wafer, are trimmed by plasma, and serve as the etch or lift-off mask for the capacitor lattice.
why: Removes the scanner from the capacitor layer; trough equipment is cheap and domestic.

title: Legacy-fab conversion fund for drop-in zero-refresh memory
idea: TRIZ #20 Continuity of useful action: a CHIPS-style program pays conversion costs plus a 5-year offtake for U.S. 200/300 mm legacy fabs (65-180 nm lines with idle tools) to run a standard refresh-free memory PDK (asymmetric-electrode AFE capacitor or self-selecting crosspoint), keeping depreciated tools productive instead of building new $15B fabs.
why: Conversion ~$0.2-0.5B per fab vs $15B+ greenfield; adds U.S. zero-refresh memory supply in ~18-24 months and offloads refresh-hungry DRAM (capital, U.S. manufacturability).

title: Four charge levels per cell doubles bits without new tools
idea: Store 2 bits per 1T1C cell as four charge levels, read by a time-to-digital sense amplifier that measures how long the bitline takes to develop rather than its polarity; same fab, same masks, same node.
why: 1.6-1.8x bits per wafer net of larger sense amps with zero new capex (Fact 4); fights the charge wall (Fact 1), hence high risk.

title: SEL's IGZO DOSRAM built on glass in shuttered LCD fabs
idea: Semiconductor Energy Laboratory's IGZO DOSRAM never found a fab, while Gen-8 to Gen-10 LCD fabs such as Sharp Sakai are closing. Retool one closed line with roll-to-plate nanoimprint at 30 nm, stack 4 layers of IGZO 2T0C gain cells on 2.2x2.5 m glass with wide landing pads that absorb glass distortion, and bond CMOS periphery chiplets along the panel edge.
why: Meets 100x: panel capex per m2 is ~1/100-1/500 of wafer fabs and already written off; est. ~$0.05-0.1/GB. Trades: low IGZO mobility (100 ns+ access), slab form factor, panel-scale imprint yield.

title: Hf: one HfZrO deposition serves gate, capacitor and liner
idea: In a vertical-channel 4F2 cell, deposit a single conformal HfZrO film that wraps the channel (gate dielectric), continues over the storage node (capacitor dielectric) and seals the stack (liner), then tune each region's phase with localized anneal.
why: Process consolidation: three dielectric modules collapse into one ALD step plus anneal, cutting tool types and cycle time ~10%.
